To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the energy dependence of damage in semiconductors is not as strong as previously thought; (2) the energy dependence is different for different properties; (3) there is a large difference between the energy dependence of recombination rate and carrier removal; (4) the energy dependence can be calculated from neutron scattering data and recoil range energy relationships; and (5) the annealing of damage is important in determining the final damage produced

the relative effectiveness of 1-MeV and 14-Mev neutrons for producing displacement damage depends on the property measured and on the annealing process, and that the relative effectiveness is larger for recombination than for carrier removal.

(a) The energy dependence of displacement damage is determined by the recoil energy spectrum, the recoil range-energy relation, and the defect production cross sections; (b) the energy dependence of displacement effects in semiconductors can be predicted from neutron-scattering and recoil-range data and the defect production data; and (c) the relative effectiveness of 1-MeV and 14-Mev neutrons can vary with the property being measured and with time after irradiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the development of an analytical model of displacement effects in semiconductors, (2) a comparison with the experimental data available, (3) the prediction of the effects of 1-MeV and 14-Mev neutrons on semiconductor properties, (4) the prediction of annealing effects, (5) the prediction of relative damage produced by different neutron spectra, and (6) the prediction of damage produced by different reactor neutron spectra.
the effects of neutron energy on the formation and evolution of defect clusters in semiconductors and the effect on macroscopic properties of the material.

the following: (1) the development of a theory of displacement production by neutrons, (2) the development of experimental techniques for the measurement of displacement production by 14-Mev neutrons, and (3) the application of these results to the understanding of the effects of neutron irradiation of semiconductors
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
14-MeVe neutrons are more effective than reactor neutrons in producing defects in Si.
the relative effectiveness of different energy neutrons is not known with certainty, but it can be estimated to a reasonable approximation.
the energy-dependence of displacement effects in semiconductors has not been established, and that it will not be until a great deal more information is available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the damage produced by 14 MeV neutrons can be described by a single damage factor for all semiconductor properties.
the energy dependence of the defect production in semiconductors is not well known.
, for a given damage factor, 14-Me V neutrons will produce more damage than reactor neutrons, and that this factor is dependent on the property measured and the time scale of measurement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy dependence of displacement effects in semiconductors can be derived directly, without recourse to any adjustable parameters, from neutron-scattering and recoil-range-energy relationships.
the relative effects of reactor and 14-Mev neutrons are not constant and can vary significantly depending on the property measured and the time scale of annealing.
the damage produced by a given number of 14-Mev neutrons is greater than that produced by an equivalent number of reactor neutrons.
